title: DAAD RISE Germany 2027 - Paid Summer Research Internships for Undergraduates

organization.about: The German Academic Exchange Service, known as DAAD, supports international academic exchange and cooperation. Based in Bonn, Germany, it provides scholarships and funding through a range of programmes for eligible students, graduates and researchers. Its work connects German universities with international partners and helps strengthen research, study and academic mobility.
organization.name: German Academic Exchange Service

stipend: €992 per month scholarship for the internship period, plus a €160 allowance for travel within Germany and an international travel allowance.
intro: DAAD RISE Germany 2027: paid summer research internships in Germany for undergraduate science and engineering students. €992 monthly stipend plus travel allowances. Apply by 30 November 2026 (11:59 pm CET).
description:
What RISE Germany Is

RISE Germany (Research Internships in Science and Engineering) is a DAAD programme that pairs undergraduate students from around the world with doctoral researchers at German universities and institutes. The interns work on a real research project for a summer - typically two to three months in 2027 - inside a working lab rather than a classroom. Placements span biology, chemistry, physics, earth sciences, engineering and computer science, and each internship is tied to a specific PhD project that a doctoral student has proposed to host an assistant.

The arrangement works both ways: the PhD student gets a motivated assistant for the summer, and the intern gets a first, honest look at what doctoral research actually involves. For students considering a research career - and especially those planning to apply for master's or PhD positions in Germany later - it is one of the most useful short experiences available.

What You Get

Scholarship components
ComponentDetails
Monthly stipend€992 per month for a full month of the internship, paid by DAAD.
Travel within Germany€160 allowance to cover local and domestic travel.
International travelAn international travel allowance is included in the scholarship package.
PlacementA matched summer research placement with a German doctoral project in summer 2027.

Eligibility and Fit

Who should apply
CriterionRequirement
Study levelEnrolled undergraduate (bachelor's) students in science, engineering or a closely related subject.
StageThe programme is aimed at students who are still completing their first degree; check the official requirements page for the exact year-of-study rules.
LanguageThe working language of RISE placements is English; German is not required.
NationalityOpen to international undergraduate students; there is no single-country restriction.

Application Dates and Process

Key dates for the 2027 round
ComponentDetails
Portal opened15 October 2026
Deadline30 November 2026, 11:59 pm CET
MatchingComplete applications are forwarded to internship providers after DAAD's review; providers may contact shortlisted applicants directly.
Internship periodSummer 2027 (typically 2-3 months, agreed with the host)

How to Apply

Applications are submitted only through the RISE Germany online database portal, which is the link on this page. After registering, candidates upload their documents and can indicate the projects that match their interests; DAAD then reviews complete applications and passes them to the hosting doctoral researchers. There is no application fee, and the entire process - matching, notification and placement - runs through the portal, so it pays to draft your documents well before the 30 November cut-off.

Why This Programme Is Worth Your Time

Germany's doctoral system is employment-based, and supervisors there place real weight on prior lab experience when hiring. A RISE summer gives you that experience with a German research group, a reference who can vouch for your lab work, and a realistic preview of the German academic environment - all while being paid. Students who complete RISE frequently go on to DAAD-funded master's study or doctoral positions in Germany.
